title: Add template CLI `doctor` command (env + API + OTel collector checks)
author: Monica Patel
release_notes: Quickstart CLI: add `doctor` command to validate local environment (API key/config), Redwood API connectivity, and OpenTelemetry collector reachability with actionable remediation hints.
description:
## Summary
This adds a `doctor` command to the quickstart CLI to help users debug the top three categories of template setup failures we’ve seen in internal beta and support: (1) missing/malformed env vars, (2) can’t reach Redwood API / auth errors, and (3) OTel exporter/collector misconfig.

`doctor` runs a lightweight set of checks and prints a short, actionable remediation for each failure (e.g., which env var is missing, whether the key looks empty/whitespace, whether the collector endpoint is unreachable, etc.). The command is safe-by-default: it never prints secrets and it redacts header values.

## CLI UX
- `redwood-quickstart doctor` (human output)
- `redwood-quickstart doctor --json` (machine-readable output for CI / scripts)
- `redwood-quickstart doctor --timeout-ms 3000` (override network timeouts)
- `redwood-quickstart doctor --skip-otel` (skip OTel checks; helpful for users not running a collector)

Example output:
- ✅ Env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY present (redacted), REDWOOD_MODEL set to `rw-verified/llama-3.1-8b-instruct`
- ✅ Redwood API: reachable (GET /v1/models, 200)
- ⚠️ OpenTelemetry: OTLP endpoint not reachable (http://localhost:4318) — start local collector via `docker compose up otel-collector` or set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT

## Checks implemented
### 1) Env/config validation
Validates presence/format of (template-agnostic) config keys:
- `REDWOOD_API_KEY` (required)
- `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` (optional; defaults to hosted)
- `REDWOOD_MODEL` (required for quickstarts; prints if unset)
- `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (optional; if set, we validate it parses as a URL)
- `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` (optional; parsed but values redacted)

Notes:
- We treat empty-string and whitespace-only values as missing.
- We avoid suggesting shell commands that echo secrets back to stdout.

### 2) API connectivity / auth
Performs a short request to validate network connectivity and credentials:
- Uses the same client construction as `init` (same env var resolution path).
- Calls a low-cost endpoint to confirm auth and base URL correctness (currently `GET /v1/models`).
- Classifies common failures into user-facing messages:
  - 401/403: "API key missing/invalid or org not authorized"
  - 404: "Base URL looks wrong (did you set REDWOOD_BASE_URL to a non-API domain?)"
  - 429: "Rate limited; reduce concurrency or wait; verify template retry/backoff"
  - Timeout/DNS: "Network/proxy issues; check egress + corporate proxy rules"

### 3) Collector health (OTLP)
If `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set (or defaults to local dev when running from template scaffolds), `doctor` verifies we can reach the collector endpoint:
- For http(s) endpoints: performs a HEAD/GET probe to the base endpoint with a short timeout.
- Emits guidance aligned with the template docs: use docker-compose local collector + verify port mappings.
- Explicitly calls out the most common misconfig we’ve seen in SUP-29422: endpoint set but missing auth headers / incorrect scheme.

## Implementation notes
- Introduces `packages/cli/src/doctor/*` with a small check framework:
  - each check returns {status, summary, details, remediation}
  - `--json` prints a stable schema for downstream tooling
- Adds redaction helpers shared with the existing logging utilities.
- Adds unit tests around env parsing + redaction + error classification.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add a "send a test trace" option once we finalize the local collector pipeline (ENG-4184 follow-up).
- Expand model validation to optionally confirm configured model exists in the account (PM-913 alignment).

- [x] Doesn’t log secrets (API key, OTLP headers)
- [x] Network calls have bounded timeouts
- [x] `--json` output is stable and documented
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Docs blurb added to CLI README

notable_snippet:
Human output format (example):

Doctor results
- ENV ................. OK
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY: set (redacted)
  - REDWOOD_MODEL: set (rw-verified/llama-3.1-8b-instruct)
- API ................. OK
  - GET /v1/models: 200 (latency=182ms)
- OTEL ................ WARN
  - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 not reachable (ECONNREFUSED)
  Remediation: start local collector via `docker compose up otel-collector` or set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to your collector URL.
review_conversation: Allison Grant: For the OTEL check, please make sure we don’t encourage users to add high-cardinality attributes in remediation text. Also confirm we never print OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS values (even in debug).
Monica Patel: Updated redaction to treat OTLP headers as secrets and only print header keys. Remediation text is now generic (no attribute suggestions), and `--json` details omit headers entirely.
Christine Wong: Can we bound all network calls with a default timeout and expose an override flag? Also ensure we don’t retry in doctor (we want deterministic + fast).
Monica Patel: Added `--timeout-ms` (default 3000) and removed any retry logic for doctor probes. API probe is single request only.
Ibrahim Khan: The API probe endpoint: /v1/models is fine but please confirm it’s cheap and doesn’t create side effects. Also classify 429 separately so we don’t tell users their key is wrong.
Monica Patel: Confirmed: GET /v1/models is read-only. Added explicit 429 handling with guidance to reduce concurrency and wait/backoff.
Sahana Iyer: Tests look good. One nit: JSON output should be stable; please include a version field so we can evolve later.
Monica Patel: Added `schema_version: 1` to the JSON formatter and documented it in README.
Allison Grant: Approved (thanks for the redaction fixes).
